item.title: How to Create a Bidirectional File Sync using Unison
item.description:
So if you came here I consider you already have a problem to solve, and you are familiar with unison. If this is the case, skip the introduction please.

If you don’t, then keep reading as it might clarify a few things before we get started with the how to use unison in order to create a bidirectional (two way) synchronization of two directories.

Introduction

To simplify the understanding let’s imagine that you have two folders and you want both folders to be synchronized when an event happens such as a new file is created, a file got changed or even a file got deleted. You want both folders to reflect exactly the same state as a replica.

item.title: Installing PHPUnit on Windows
item.description:
Hello person(s), today I’ll present a step-by-step guide to installing PHPUnit on Uncle Bil Gates’ famous operating system, Microsoft Windows 7 (Seven), before continuing with the tutorial I wanted to talk a little about unit tests and test-driven development (the famous TDD – Test Driven Development).

So, what is TDD?

TDD is a method for building software, not just testing it. Through the “Red”, “Green”, “Refactoring” process, you notice that the code becomes clean, organized and best of all, working!

item.title: Installing ZeosLib in Delphi XE2
item.description:
After having difficulty installing ZeosLib in Delphi XE2, I decided to share “the way through”.

The ZeosLib Library

The ZeosLib library consists of a set of tools so you can have a native database connection, meaning a connection without auxiliary drivers such as ODBC.

ZeosLib is an open-source project, its installation isn’t that complex, but here’s the recipe, just follow the steps without skipping “any ingredient”.
